one_liner: Std-only Rust JavaScript engine with an ARM64 template JIT; about 2.2x QuickJS on V8-v7 on Apple Silicon, slower on x86-64.
what_it_does: A from-scratch, full-spec JavaScript engine (passes all 53,400 test262 tests per its README) with a tree-walking reference interpreter, a bytecode VM and a template JIT, plus a Node/Deno-style runtime (event loop, timers, fs, fetch over plain http, node: compatibility, N-API addons). It is not a QuickJS drop-in: the engine is a Rust workspace with an embedding API behind the `embed` feature, or you run the `lumen` / `lumen-cli` binaries from the rolling nightly release.
how_it_is_fast: Bytecode functions get per-site inline caches backed by object shapes (hidden classes) and dense-array fast paths; on ARM64 the template JIT bakes those cache reads into the machine code, fuses compare-and-branch, and keeps runs of arithmetic in floating-point registers ('numeric register chains'). A separate numeric-loop backend finds closed numeric loops in the control-flow graph, gives up to eight locals fixed FP register homes, and writes state back at guarded exits. A liveness pass moves values at their last use instead of cloning them, which matters because values are reference-counted with a cycle collector.
when_to_use: Embedding a full-spec JS engine in a Rust program with zero third-party dependencies, running on Apple Silicon or Linux arm64.
Numeric-loop-heavy scripts on ARM64, where the JIT wins big: Richards, Crypto and NavierStokes score about 9x QuickJS on the macOS arm64 runner.
You need spec completeness (Intl, Temporal, Proxy, modules, full RegExp) that small embeddable engines lack, and can trade binary size for it.
Experimenting with a hackable, safe-Rust engine whose three tiers are cross-checked by a differential fuzzer.
when_not_to_use: x86-64 hosts: on the Ubuntu runner lumen scores 444 against QuickJS 1217 and loses all eight V8-v7 subtests, because the x86-64 JIT backend is 'correctness-first' with checked per-op helpers.

Object-, GC- or string-heavy code: even on arm64 it loses RayTrace, EarleyBoyer and Splay to QuickJS; the maintainers' own docs put a Djot parser at about 15.5x Node's time, and issue #12 timed a yt-dlp ejs script at 55.80 minutes against QuickJS's 8.20 seconds (July 2026).
You need JIT-class speed: the authors' Apple M4 runs give a V8-v7 composite of about 8,560, about 9.7x below Node 24 and 11x below Bun.
Size-constrained targets: the release binary is about 8 to 11 MB (about 3 MB of CLDR data unless built with --no-default-features), versus about 1 MB for QuickJS.
Windows or https: no nightly Windows build (issue #22 open), and fetch rejects https URLs.

integration.form: Rust workspace used as a git dependency (not published to crates.io; the crates.io name 'lumen' is an unrelated tool) or prebuilt CLI binaries
integration.platforms: ARM64 JIT on macOS, Linux and Windows; correctness-first x86-64 JIT on macOS, Linux and Windows; other architectures fall back to the bytecode VM; nightly binaries for macOS arm64/x86_64 and Linux x86_64/arm64 only
integration.thread_safety: Engine is !Send; the runtime gives one loop thread ownership of the engine and runs blocking work on a std thread pool

gotchas: The speedup over QuickJS is architecture-dependent: on the same 2026-10-05 shootout lumen is 2.24x QuickJS on macos-arm64 but 0.36x on ubuntu x86-64, so benchmark on your own target.

The composite is a geometric mean, and the arm64 win comes from three numeric subtests at about 9x; the suite's Richards fixture is part of lumen's own JIT CI, so the engine is tuned on this benchmark.

The shootout runs each engine once per platform per day on shared GitHub runners; the macOS runner score (3953) is less than half of the authors' Apple M4 score (about 8,560), so absolute numbers move with runner hardware.

Memory is reference counting plus cycle collection, and the JIT maps executable memory through raw mmap/mprotect or VirtualAlloc declarations; unsafe code is concentrated in the JIT templates and the N-API loader.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick lumen over Porffor when you need a full-spec engine that runs arbitrary JS (test262-complete, modules, Intl) rather than an AOT compiler, and over lo or LLRT when you want a pure-Rust, dependency-free engine rather than a V8- or QuickJS-based runtime; for speed on x86-64 none of these beats plain QuickJS by lumen's route.
verified_claims_summary: In ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark's daily GitHub Actions run of the classic V8-v7 suite (snapshot 2026-10-05), the lumen nightly 0.1.3 (f6c9860, rustc stable, opt-level 3, fat LTO, codegen-units 1, panic=abort per lumen's Cargo.toml and nightly.yml) scored 3953 against QuickJS 2026.06.04's 1761 on the macos-latest arm64 runner, but 444 against 1217 on the ubuntu-latest x86-64 runner; runner CPU models are not recorded and each engine runs once.
status_note: Very active (last commit 2026-09-24, 0.1.x, MIT) and copyable, but young: real applications still run 15x or more slower than Node, the fast JIT paths are ARM64-only, and it is not published as a library crate.
